judged_text: The automatic-group guard spec drives remove_member with `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` even though routes.rb wires that action only under `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (its sibling test three lines below correctly uses `xhr :delete`), and because rspec-rails controller specs dispatch by action name without consulting routes.rb, the suite validates the action through a request shape production can never make. Any routing regression on the new member endpoints — a flipped verb, renamed action, or dropped route in config/routes.rb — passes the entire suite while the admin UI's real `type: "DELETE"`/`type: "PUT"` calls to /admin/groups/:group_id/members.json (group.js removeMember/addMembers) start returning 404/500 in production; the in-diff :put/:delete inconsistency shows these specs no longer mirror the HTTP contract they claim to verify.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `config/routes.rb` wires `remove_member` only to `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, while `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` contains `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` in the automatic-group guard test. Because controller specs invoke the action directly (and `remove_member` in `Admin::GroupsController` does not check the HTTP verb), this test can pass despite using a verb/route combination that cannot occur in production, reducing coverage of the actual HTTP contract for the new member endpoints. This is a test reliability/coverage issue rather than a runtime bug in the app logic shown in the diff.
